messages:
julia: Hey team — customer (AcmePayments) reports 401s from our Node/TS SDK only after bundling for Next.js Edge. Local `next dev` and plain Node repros are fine. Happening in prod edge runtime after deploy. Repro steps pasted below. @samir can you triage?

samir: on it. quick q — which SDK version and which bundler (turbopack/esbuild/webpack)?

julia: SDK v1.4.7, Next 14 edge runtime, turbopack in their pipeline but they also tried esbuild standalone (same result). They mentioned the bundle size shrank a lot after tree-shaking.

anna: can you paste the error? stack/logs?

julia: sure — this is what their edge function logs show when trying to call our API: `fetch failed: 401 Unauthorized` then our server log shows `invalid auth: missing Authorization header` despite the SDK sending an ApiKey in local runs. In built bundle the outgoing request headers are missing the Authorization header.

mike: interesting — could be packaging/conditional exports causing the edge build to pull a browser shim or ESM build that doesn't attach headers the same way. I've seen bundlers rewrite `globalThis` access.

julia: repro steps they gave:
1) clone repo
2) `npm i @redwood/inference@1.4.7`
3) create `pages/api/edge.ts` with:
```ts
import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference';
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY });
export default async function handler(req) {
  const r = await client.text.generate({ model: 'gpt-small', input: 'hi' });
  return new Response(JSON.stringify(r));
}
```
4) `next build && next start` => request to edge route returns 401.

samir: do they get different code when inspecting the built `.next` artifacts vs node_modules? Can they check `node_modules/@redwood/inference/package.json` inside the final bundle?

julia: they unpacked `.next/server/chunks/` and found our SDK entry replaced with `dist/index.mjs` (ESM) but types field missing from the package copied into the chunk. Their bundle also shows `require` wrapper removed.

eng-packaging-bot: note: this smells like conditional exports + bundler preferring `import` over `require` and accidentally pulling our browser/lightweight runtime variant. See https://redwood.dev/packaging-guides (internal).

mike: quick check — our package.json currently has: "exports": { ".": { "import": "./dist/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/index.cjs" }, "./browser": "./dist/browser.mjs" }, "types": "dist/index.d.ts"
If a bundler inlines the module, it might prefer the `import` path and then tree-shake code paths that attach headers. We also have an `if (isBrowser)` branch that avoids Node headers for runtime detection — bundlers sometimes evaluate that at build time.

anna: could be Terser/rollup/tree-shake evaluating `typeof window` or `process` and removing Node-specific header code. Also the SDK uses a tiny runtime detection helper: `const isEdge = typeof EdgeRuntime !== 'undefined' || /edge/.test(process.env.NEXT_RUNTIME || '');` If bundlers substitute `NEXT_RUNTIME` at build-time, the branch could flip.

samir: we need a quick repro on our side. I'll try to reproduce in a minimal Next Edge app with turbopack.

support-bot: escalation created: #ESCL-2247 assigned to samir, priority high, customer impacted: prod 401s.

julia: customer also tried forcing `require('@redwood/inference').RedwoodClient` in their code — same result. They said `Authorization` header present in browser devtools when using `fetch` to their edge route, but missing in the outgoing request from the edge runtime to our API. So the SDK probably alters the fetch/headers behavior in that variant.

mike: workaround idea — ask customer to pin `@redwood/inference@1.4.4` (older build that shipped only CJS) and see if that fixes headers. Also suggest adding an explicit header: `client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY, forceInjectHeader: true })` — we don't currently have that option but could ask them to shim by setting `globalThis.__REDWOOD_API_KEY = process.env.RW_API_KEY` before requiring the SDK (hacky).

samir: I'm reproducing now. initial findings: turbopack resolves `import` path to `dist/index.mjs`. The `dist/index.mjs` build uses `if (typeof process === 'undefined')` checks which at bundle-time the packer resolves to true for edge and removes header injection code. So server-side header attach code is behind a branch that got pruned.

mike: that matches. Longer-term fix: avoid runtime feature-detection branches that bundlers can constant-fold. Replace with explicit environment check or expose dual entrypoints that guarantee header attach logic present in edge build. Eg change exports map:
```json
"exports": {".": {"edge": "./dist/index.edge.mjs", "import": "./dist/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/index.cjs"}}
```
and ship `index.edge.mjs` that keeps header logic.

anna: for immediate customer relief, recommend: 1) pin to v1.4.4 or 1.4.5 where the CJS path is used; 2) OR add a tiny server-side wrapper: `import realClient from '@redwood/inference/dist/index.cjs';` (deep import) — warns about subpath but works; 3) OR bundle config: set `resolve.conditions = ['require', 'node']` for bundler so it picks CJS.

julia: customer tried deep import (`@redwood/inference/dist/index.cjs`) and that worked — headers present and 200 returned. They want an official fix.

samir: I'll open a tracking issue and patch release. Plan: 1) create `index.edge.mjs` that explicitly avoids build-time-remove branches, 2) update packaging to include explicit `edge` condition in `exports` with preserved header logic, 3) add an integration test: Next.js Edge build in CI.

mike: also add a note in README about bundlers and conditional exports + a suggested `next.config.js` snippet:
```js
module.exports = { experimental: { esmExternals: 'loose' }, webpack: (cfg) => { cfg.resolve.conditions = ['node', 'require']; return cfg; } }
```

eng-packaging-bot: creating release branch `packaging/edge-exports-fix` and adding CI job `edge-packaging-test`.

samir: filed internal issue: INF-7889, linked to customer case, preparing v1.4.8 patch. Will backport minimal change to prevent branch pruning.

julia: customer asks for ETA — can we ship a patch today?

samir: aiming for patch within 24h. will try to get a hotfix release (1.4.8) that reintroduces CJS-compatible runtime or explicit edge entry. If not possible today, provide customer the deep-import workaround and suggested pin.

mike: note for later: audit other packages for similar `isBrowser` style branches. Could be a recurring packaging hazard.

julia: thanks team. I'll update customer with workaround + ETA and mark escalation as notified. :thumbsup:
